text:
Eli: FYI saw a customer escalation — ACME reported chat latency spikes. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms, p99 ~1.4s since ~13:40 UTC. No error rates.

Sasha: oof. which model/route?

Eli: hosted /v1/chat generative-x-3, route model=gen-x-3-lr. Region us-west1. Sequence lengths typical (~256).

Arjun: any infra events? NVidia driver or infra incidents?

Oncall Bot: No matching infra alerts in the last 2h. GPU utilization normal, queue depth up ~2x on pool-gw-03.

Maya: can you paste an example request (sanitized) and client replay ID?

Eli: request sample: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat -d '{"model":"gen-x-3-lr","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summary of Q1"}]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
replay_id: replay-2026-03-17-13-46-acme-01

Kim: looking at traces — traces for that replay show an extra 800ms in serve step "attn_kern_dispatch" before token generation starts.

Sasha: attn_kern_dispatch — kernel selection heuristics. Did we recently change compile flags or kernel ordering?

Arjun: I rolled an update to the heuristic table yesterday (reduce SDPA preference for long sequences). Change-id: cfg-heuristic-20260316. It should prefer FlashAttn on compatible models but fallback to SDPA for some shapes.

Maya: could the heuristic be incorrectly selecting a slower SDPA kernel for short sequences?

Kim: logs show selected_kernel=sdpa_2x, alt=flashattn; exec_time_est=0.94 vs flashattn_est=0.28. That looks reversed; estimates look swapped.

Sasha: if estimates are wrong the runtime might pick a suboptimal kernel. Any recent changes to the cost model?

Arjun: cost model update included a normalization tweak to account for kv-cache misses. I might have messed up unit scale (ms vs us). Will roll back the normalization change to test.

Eli: can we do a quick mitigation for ACME? Maybe force route to prefer flashattn on their dedicated pool or set kernel_override for that model.

Oncall Bot: Actionable: set kernel_override=flashattn for model gen-x-3-lr on tag=acme-prod. I can apply a hot override if someone approves.

Maya: approve. Do it.

Arjun: applying override now to pool gw-03 for tag acme-prod...

deploy-bot: kernel_override flashattn applied to gw-03 (rolling 3 nodes).

Kim: preliminary telemetry — p95 down to ~150ms within 90s, p99 ~320ms. Customer notified that we applied a kernel override.

Eli: ACME confirmed improvement. They saw ~95% reduction in tail latency for that replay. :thumbsup:

Sasha: still need root cause. Arjun, keep the rollback of cost-model change in your queue and open a PR to add unit tests for cost-scale.

Arjun: will open PR and revert normalization patch. Also adding a canary test that checks kernel ranking isn't inverted for typical sequence lengths.

Maya: please include repro steps in the issue: sample replay id, curl, exact env var toggles, and the kernel selection logs.

Kim: repro steps I used:
1) export RW_SIM_SEQ=256 RW_MODEL=gen-x-3-lr
2) run ./runtime/bin/kerneldriver --replay replay-2026-03-17-13-46-acme-01 --log-kernel-selection > sel.log
3) grep 'selected_kernel' sel.log

Eli: for the hotfix timeline: override applied 13:48 UTC, full improvement 13:50 UTC, keep override until PR merges.

Oncall Bot: Note: schedule a controlled rollback only after QA signoff.

Sasha: also check if compile flags were changed during last bake (LTO/fastmath?). Sometimes compile optimizations change perf characteristics for FlashAttn kernels.

Arjun: compile flags unchanged in last month for that artifact. But I'll re-run microbenchmarks of both kernels with current flags.

Maya: Support follow-up: send ACME a short summary and ETA on permanent fix (estimate 48h). I'll own the customer message.

Eli: thanks team. File an incident ticket with labels: p99-latency, kernel-selection, customer-escalation, hotfix-applied.

Kim: incident created: INC-2026-1034. Attaching sel.log and perf traces.

Arjun: PR opened to revert normalization and add tests: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4821

Sasha: nice. Once PR merges, we'll remove kernel_override and monitor for regression for 1h.

Maya: customer update sent. They appreciated the quick patch.

Eli: closing loop — will follow up postmortem once the PR merges with a short note on how to avoid similar cost-model unit mixups.
